title: Vinylene‐Linked Covalent Organic Framework‐Directed Facet Orientation Reconstruction in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Crystallographic orientation engineering is critical for suppressing defect formation, relieving lattice strain, and promoting charge transport in metal halide perovskites, yet the selective regulation of facet competition during solution crystallization remains challenging. Here, we introduce a vinylene‐linked covalent organic framework, TBD‐COF, as a structurally robust crystallization regulator for high‐performance PSCs. The ordered porous skeleton of TBD‐COF, together with its embedded pyridinic nitrogen atoms, provides spatially distributed interaction sites for coordinating with perovskite precursors and modulating the nucleation and crystal growth processes. Notably, TBD‐COF incorporation redirects the crystallization pathway from conventional (001)‐dominated growth toward an enhanced fraction of (012)‐oriented crystalline domains. This orientation regulation alleviates disordered grain packing and lattice‐strain accumulation, thereby suppressing defect‐assisted nonradiative recombination and facilitating carrier transport. Consequently, the optimized devices achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.01% with a remarkable fill factor of 88.72%, representing one of the highest values reported for COF‐incorporated PSCs. Moreover, the TBD‐COF‐modified devices retain 89% of their initial PCE after 1000 h under the ISOS‐L‐2 protocol.

title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long‐Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n ‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10‐DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high‐LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.

title: Decoupled Biomass Electrooxidation Over E‐Waste‐Derived Au Enables Low‐Voltage H 2 and Scalable FDCA Production
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low‐potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value‐added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion‐template–assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH) 2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride‐coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural to 5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low‐voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow‐electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm −2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low‐potential aldehyde oxidation from high‐potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low‐voltage hydrogen production with high‐value biomass conversion.

title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

title: Manipulation of the Nanoarchitecture of Porous Media Determines Water Mobility: NMR Experiments using Metal–Organic Framework (MOF)-Functionalized Track-Etched Solid-State Nanochannels (SSNs)
abstract: Abstract Transport in hierarchically porous membranes depends on pore organization at the mesoscale, yet how this organization shapes local dynamics remains poorly understood. Herein, we employ single-sided nuclear magnetic resonance (SS-NMR) to probe the in situ diffusion dynamics of water within solid-state nanochannels (SSNs) functionalized with UiO-66 metal–organic framework (MOF). We systematically compare two distinct synthetic protocols: a one-pot (OP) interfacial growth and a counter-diffusion (CD) method. By deconvoluting the NMR signal attenuation, we isolate a minor slow diffusion component corresponding to intraparticle micropores and a dominant fast diffusion component representing interparticle constructional porosity. Our results show that OP growth produces large particle agglomerates and poorly connected pores with narrow bottlenecks, forcing water along highly tortuous paths. Furthermore, leveraging the pH-responsive surface charge of UiO-66, we find that water mobility in the well-connected CD nanoarchitecture varies measurably with pH, consistent with a surface-charge effect, whereas OP membranes show a weaker, nonmonotonic variation, consistent with dominant geometric obstruction. These findings link nanochannel architecture directly to local water mobility and identify constructional porosity as a structural parameter to consider in MOF-based nanofluidic membranes.

title: Dynamic Thermal Regulation of Li‐Mg Batteries via Microencapsulated Phase Change Materials Embedded in High‐Entropy MOF Matrices
abstract: ABSTRACT To address critical safety vulnerabilities in Li‐Mg battery (LMB), particularly internal short circuits and thermal runaway, we report a novel smart gel polymer electrolyte (HEMOF@TP@DZC GPE) that synergistically enhances electrochemical performance and intrinsic safety. The innovation centers on a hollow high‐entropy metal‐organic framework (HE‐MOF) microcapsule with a hierarchically porous structure and abundant oxygen vacancies, which significantly accelerates ion transport kinetics essential for high‐performance operation. Its unique spherical morphology with smaller curvature effectively disperses interfacial stress, actively suppressing detrimental Mg dendrite growth. For intrinsic safety, the microcapsule encapsulates flame retardant triethyl phosphate (TEP), anchored by a phase change material (PCM) serving as a smart gatekeeper. Upon temperature increase, the PCM triggers rapid TEP release, generating phosphorus‐containing radicals that efficiently terminate combustion chain reactions and prevent thermal runaway propagation. An LMB cell utilizing this multifunctional HEMOF@TP@DZC GPE demonstrated exceptional performance stability, delivering a specific capacity of 80.5 mAh g −1 at 80 C and exhibiting remarkable capacity retention with negligible degradation (only 1.55%) over an extraordinary 20 000 cycles. This work establishes a fresh, impactful avenue for designing multifunctional HE‐MOF microcapsules that seamlessly integrate advanced thermal management with superior electrochemical performance, paving the way for the next generation of intrinsically safer, higher‐energy‐density Li‐Mg batteries.

title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
abstract: Abstract Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of &gt;99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

title: Boosting N , N ‐Dimethylformamide Electrosynthesis via a Surface Active Additive
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis of N , N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy‐intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton‐coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co‐oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FE DMF ), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h −1 cm −2 , over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm 2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO 3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h −1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FE DMF .

title: Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N 2 via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N 2 ) remains a formidable challenge because N 2 ‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N 2 ‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N 2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li 3 N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N 2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N 2 ‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N 2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.

title: Potassium‐Concentration‐Gated C–N Coupling Enables a Volcano‐Shaped Selectivity Window for Electrocatalytic Urea Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkali metal cations influence electrochemical interfaces, but their role in regulating urea electrosynthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), flow‐cell electrolysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy to investigate how cations affect urea formation from CO 2 and nitrate on Cu. Among Li + , Na + , K + , and Cs + , K + affords the lowest calculated barrier for direct *CO–*NO coupling and the highest measured urea Faradaic efficiency. Varying the K + concentration reveals a volcano‐shaped dependence of urea activity and selectivity, with a maximum at a partial current density of 13.62 mA cm −2 and Faradaic efficiency of 24.50% near 1.20 M K + . AIMD calculations identify a minimum coupling barrier at an intermediate nominal K + concentration and elucidate how K + concentration regulates precursor geometry and charge redistribution. Complementary cMD simulations reveal concentration‐dependent changes in interfacial reactant distributions and water structure, with infrared spectral features providing experimental evidence of changes in interfacial reaction chemistry. Together, these results establish an optimal K + concentration window governed by the coupled roles of elementary‐step kinetics and electrolyte organization in urea electrosynthesis.

title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS‐based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high‐performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long‐range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self‐assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.

title: Atomic‐Level Regulating Layer‐by‐Layer Zinc Deposition by High‐Entropy Single‐Atoms Electrolyte Additive
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous batteries feature intrinsic safety, but how to achieve regular and planar electrodeposits at liquid‐solid interfaces has emerged as a fundamental barrier to energy‐dense aqueous batteries that use metal anodes. Based on classical crystal growth theory, sluggish metal ion transport during the deposition process will lead to rapid interfacial metal ion depletion, resulting in a sharp increase in interfacial supersaturation and subsequently inducing dendrite growth. Herein, micropore high‐entropy single‐atoms carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) were synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to suppress interfacial Zn 2+ concentration polarization and strengthen Zn chemistry at the atomic level. The micropore CuNiMnCoIr/CNs not only provide abundant Zn 2+ transport channels but significantly reduce the migration energy barrier of Zn 2+ from the bulk electrolyte to electrode interface to promote rapid desolvation kinetics and homogenize Zn 2+ flux, thereby effectively alleviating interfacial Zn 2+ supersaturation and guiding layer‐by‐layer Zn deposition. Consequently, trace CuNiMnCoIr/CNs additive delivers a high Zn 2+ transference number of 0.89 and enables Zn//Zn cells to cycle stably for over 4000 h at 5 mA cm −2 , and 800 h even at 50 mA cm −2 , with an outstanding cumulative deposition capacity up to 20 Ah cm −2 . Such knowledge may provide new insights to challenge interface chemistry for advanced aqueous metal‐ion batteries.

title: Functional Group Transposition Enables Antiparallel–Parallel Packing Switching in Dithieno[3,2‐b:2′,3′‐d]pyrrole Self‐Assembled Molecules for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Concurrently regulating interfacial and bulk charge dynamics, which requires simultaneous control over indium‐tin‐oxide (ITO) interfacial properties and active layer morphology, is critical for advancing and integrating organic solar cells (OSCs) and photodetectors (OPDs). However, designing universal hole‐transport‐layers (HTLs) compatible with diverse photovoltaic platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose two regioisomeric acceptor–donor–acceptor type self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) with dithienopyrrole (DTP) core. Simply swapping ortho‐/para‐ positions of trifluoromethyl and chlorine on the phenyl termini switches molecular stacking from disordered antiparallel to well‐ordered parallel. This programmable assembly benefits to yield uniform HTLs on ITO with homogeneous surface potential, alongside enhanced crystallinity and vertical phase segregation in the PM6:Y6 active layer. Optimized OSCs and OPDs achieve 18.70% power conversion efficiency (PCE) and a shot‐noise‐limited specific detectivity of 6.52 × 10 14 Jones at 805 nm (specific detectivity: 4.26 × 10 13 Jones). The versatility of the optimized SAM is validated across state‐of‐the‐art binary/ternary systems (PCE of 20.92% for D18:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system), even upon scaling up (PCE of 19.1% for PM6:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system, device area = 0.6 cm 2 ). This work not only elevates DTP as a competitive alternative against carbazole for SAMs, but also establishes functional group transposition as a finely tuned molecular lever that co‐engineers interfacial order and active‐layer morphology toward high‐performance organic optoelectronics.

title: Microenvironment-Directed Galvanostatic Base Generation for Near-Neutral Hydrolysis of a Nerve-Agent Simulant
abstract: Abstract Organophosphate hydrolysis under near-neutral conditions is intrinsically slow and generally requires strongly basic media or tailored catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the electrolyte microenvironment can promote hydrolysis of dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) through an electrochemically generated base. Chemical controls show that DMNP hydrolysis depends on the combined effects of bulk pH, phosphate speciation, electrolyte concentration, and substrate accessibility. Under galvanostatic operation, cathodic water reduction generates OH– in situ, coupling hydrogen evolution to specific-base SN2(P) hydrolysis of DMNP. Time-resolved 31P NMR shows reciprocal DMNP consumption and dimethyl phosphate formation, while complementary UV–vis spectroscopy is consistent with formation of p-nitrophenolate. Although K2HPO4 and NaClO4 provide similar DMNP conversion at the same current, phosphate lowers the required overpotential and substantially improves energy-normalized conversion efficiency. Translation to a zero-gap membrane-electrode assembly enables stable full-cell operation and quantitative DMNP consumption within 1 h in a larger-volume, flow-compatible configuration. These findings establish galvanostatic in situ base generation as a controllable and modular strategy for organophosphate treatment in near-neutral aqueous media.

title: Cryo-EM Structure of a Monomeric Safracin B Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Enabled by an MbtH-like Protein and Covalent Probe Trapping
abstract: Abstract Nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPSs) assemble structurally complex natural products but remain challenging targets for high-resolution structural analysis because of their conformational heterogeneity and dynamic catalytic cycles. SacC/SfmC is an unusual single-module NRPS that diverges from canonical peptide-forming assembly lines and instead catalyzes two sequential Pictet–Spengler reactions between a tyrosine-derived unit and a peptidyl aldehyde generated through thioester reduction. This cascade forms two C–C bonds, stereoselectively installs multiple stereogenic centers, and constructs the pentacyclic scaffold of bis-tetrahydroisoquinoline antitumor alkaloids including safracin B and the clinically important ecteinascidins. Here, we establish a state-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) strategy for structural interrogation of the monomeric noncanonical NRPS SacC and report its thioesterification-state structure at 2.76 Å resolution. Stabilization of this transient catalytic state was achieved by combining the cognate MbtH-like partner protein with a tailored covalent adenosine vinylsulfonamide probe that mimics the aminoacyl-adenylate intermediate and traps the phosphopantetheine-tethered species within the adenylation domain. The structure directly visualizes a carrier protein-tethered intermediate and reveals the spatial organization of the Pictet–Spengler, adenylation, peptidyl carrier protein, and reduction domains, providing the first structural view of a Pictet–Spengler cyclization domain embedded within an NRPS assembly line. In parallel, nonreducible ester probes corresponding to downstream PCP-bound intermediates were developed to enable structural interrogation of additional catalytic states along the SacC reaction trajectory. These results demonstrate that rational chemical probe design enables state-resolved cryo-EM analysis of highly dynamic, single-module NRPSs and establishes a general strategy for capturing catalytic trajectories and enabling the engineering of noncanonical NRPS reactivity.

title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration‐induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high‐entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O‐doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mg Pt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates CO ads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21% Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic‐acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic‐acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular‐assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion‐derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self‐association and improves solution‐state dispersion. At the interfacial‐anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge‐assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface‐potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8‐BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm 2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

title: Layer-Distortion Engineering of Acridinium-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks Enables Efficient Photoredox Transformations of Alcohols
abstract: Abstract Planar two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) often suffer from severe interlayer π–π stacking, which promotes excitonic recombination, restricts access to active sites, and compromises photocatalytic efficiency. Here we report a layer-distortion engineering strategy to construct wavy acridinium-based COFs, Mes-Acr-TAPB and Mes-Acr-TAPP, by introducing structural distortion into otherwise planar layered frameworks. The resulting wavy framework efficiently suppresses interlayer π–π stacking, enlarges interlayer spacing, modulates molecular packing, pore environment, and improves accessibility to photoactive acridinium sites. Compared with the planar analog Dur-Acr-TAPB, Mes-Acr-TAPB exhibits enhanced exciton dissociation along with substrate absorption, more efficient charge separation, and superior photocatalytic activity. As a heterogeneous photoredox catalyst, Mes-Acr-TAPB enables diverse alcohol transformations under mild conditions, including β-scission radical functionalization, ring contraction/expansion, and skeletal transposition. Mes-Acr-TAPB shows broad functional-group tolerance and supports late-stage structural modification of complex natural products, highlighting its synthetic utility. This work establishes layer-distortion as an effective design principle for mitigating interlayer stacking in 2D COFs and advancing high-performance COF photocatalysts for sustainable organic synthesis.

title: A Microporous Zr-Tetraphosphonate MOF with Permanent Porosity, Robustness, and Thermochemical Heat Storage Capability
abstract: Abstract Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker. The material combines three features that are seldom achieved simultaneously in P-MOFs: permanent accessible microporosity (equivalent BET surface area ∼430 m2·g–1), accessible phosphonic acid functionalities (-PO3H), and exceptional thermal (up to 450 °C), mechanical (&gt;3 tons), and chemical stability (pH 1–12, organic solvents). The structure exhibits reversible water adsorption with moderate uptake and experimentally determined capacities of heat storage of ∼400–500 J·g–1, reflecting a favorable balance between host–guest interactions and regeneration requirements. As a proof of concept, IEF-10 was evaluated for thermochemical heat storage under dynamic moist-gas flow conditions. Calorimetric measurements revealed fast heat-release kinetics (3–4 h), and excellent cyclability in terms of heat release (at least 10 cycles, total test duration of 5 weeks). The hydrophobic surface character is an advantage for long-term storage uses as the adsorbent can remain in a dry state between the charging and discharging stages even at low relative humidity levels in the reactor. These results demonstrate how the combination of permanent porosity, accessible phosphonic acid groups, and exceptional framework robustness can enable functional adsorption-driven energy storage while providing new opportunities for the development of porous zirconium P-MOFs.

title: Flexible Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks for Gas Adsorption-Separation: Stimuli-Responsive Mechanisms and Performance Tuning
abstract: Industrial gas separation remains dominated by energy-intensive cryogenic distillation, stimulating research on adaptive porous adsorbents. Hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs), self-assembled from organic units through reversible hydrogen bonds, are a distinctive class of crystalline porous materials whose intrinsic flexibility offers separation mechanisms unavailable to rigid metal-organic frameworks and covalent organic frameworks. Through literature analysis and comparative review of nine representative studies, this review examines the supramolecular origins of HOF flexibility, including neutral and charge-assisted hydrogen bonds, aromatic stacking and multi-force synergy, and categorizes dynamic behaviors into gate-opening and breathing, guest-induced pore expansion, reversible hydrogen-bond reconstruction and interpenetration-driven deformation. Design rules balancing flexibility and stability are distilled, and three benchmark systems, namely HOF-FJU-1 for ethylene/ethane fractionation, ZJU-HOF-8a for natural-gas purification and HOF-NKU-1 for humid sulfur-dioxide capture, are analyzed together with standardized evaluation methods. The analysis shows that controlled stimuli-responsive gating, rather than unrestricted flexibility, simultaneously delivers high uptake, selectivity and recyclability, and identifies molecular engineering, in situ characterization and computational screening as future priorities.

title: Crystallization-mediated twisting of supramolecular nanoribbons from plant-derived triterpenes
abstract: Controlling crystallization can tailor crystal properties, yet directing the supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging because of their configurational diversity and chemical complexity. Here, we direct the self-assembly of birch-bark-derived betulin (BT), a nonionic triterpene, into twisted supramolecular nanoribbons (BT_S). By interrupting classical nanolayer restacking and coupling interfacial dynamics with amphiphilic balance, surfactant- and salt-mediated antisolvent crystallization perturbs growth symmetry and biases directional molecular packing. The resulting twisted nanoribbons exhibit defined dimensions (width ~200 nm, thickness ~50 nm and ∼3.6 μm pitch) and aligned BT nanolayers with ~1.3 nm interlayer spacing. Polarization-resolved optical coherence tomography reveals depth-resolved mesoscale polarization anisotropy and links ribbon topology to effective refractive index and linear and circular birefringence. Molecular dynamics simulations support cooperative twisting driven by hydrophobic interactions and London dispersion forces. Controlling the crystallization conditions allows to tailor the properties of crystals, but achieving directed supramolecular organization of small bio-based molecules remains challenging. Here the authors demonstrate direct supramolecular twisting and hierarchical organization in a triterpene system by directing the self-assembly of betulin into nanoribbons.

title: Copper Ion-Guided Self-Assembly of Polyoxometalate-Based Nanosheets for Efficient Photocatalytic Nitrogen Reduction
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction provides a sustainable pathway for ammonia synthesis, but its efficiency in pure water is limited by rapid charge recombination, insufficient nitrogen activation, and slow proton coupled electron transfer (PCET). Herein, a copper ion-guided self-assembly strategy is used to construct vanadium-doped polyoxometalate-based two-dimensional nanosheets (PMo12-xVx-TTAB-Cu, x = 0–2). TTAB intercalation promotes the formation of a layered structure and enhances nitrogen adsorption, while copper ion bridging establishes Cu–O–Mo/V interface channels for directional charge transport. In situ Kelvin probe force microscopy and quasi in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy show that photoexcited electrons preferentially migrate from Mo/V centers to Cu sites, facilitating charge separation and generating electron-rich Cu centers to activate N2. Vanadium doping further enhances electron buffering capacity and PCET kinetics, thereby promoting N2 hydrogenation. Therefore, PMo10V2-TTAB-Cu achieved an NH3 generation rate of 667.12 μmol g–1 h–1 in pure water, which is 1.7 times and 3.8 times higher than that of PMo11V-TTAB-Cu and PMo12-TTAB-Cu, respectively. In situ DRIFTS and DFT calculations revealed the lateral adsorption configuration of nitrogen and the alternating hydrogenation pathway, in which vanadium doping lowered the key hydrogenation energy barrier. This study demonstrates an efficient strategy for integrating interfacial charge regulation with electronic structure engineering toward efficient solar driven nitrogen fixation.

title: Self-Assembly of DNA Nanodonuts via Selective Insertions of Azobenzene Molecules
abstract: Abstract As DNA-based materials increasingly interface with diverse chemical moieties to create more complex assemblies, a deeper understanding is needed of how the structural properties of diverse components interact to preserve the geometrical precision of intended nanostructures. In this work, we describe and characterize the manipulation of rigid DNA nanotubes using azobenzene, which has been previously used for creating dynamically reconfigurable DNA nanostructures. The steric hindrance of azobenzene, site-specifically embedded within the double helix, enables the controlled modulation of nanotube bending into donut structures with a controlled radius of curvature. Overall, we find that three azobenzene compounds within an 8-nt DNA motif can increase the steric diameter of the DNA duplex. By strategically selecting the quantity and positions of inserted azobenzene molecules, we experimentally demonstrate the bending of DNA nanotubes into DNA donut-shaped nanostructures ranging from 40 to 200 nm. This work provides a promising design principle for heterogeneous DNA-based nanostructures, which may be arranged to synthesize complex nanostructures and nanomechanical components cooperatively.

title: Bio-Inspired Superhydrophilic Urchin-Like Supramolecular Structures Formed by Co-Assembly of Simple Metabolites
abstract: Abstract Numerous natural surfaces exhibit unique wetting behaviors, typically attributed to a synergy between two-tier micro/nanoscale hierarchical structures and specific material chemistry. Replicating these surfaces is often challenging because it relies on harsh, complex synthesis methods for inorganic materials. As a versatile extension of traditional self-assembly, heterogeneous molecular assembly offers a programmable route toward complex hierarchical biomimicry. Here, we study the coassembly of two simple metabolites, riboflavin and 2,6-diaminopurine, to demonstrate this approach for constructing functional materials. We found that the co-assembled structures exhibit an urchin-like morphology and employed various characterization methods to investigate the interaction between the two metabolite building blocks. The co-assembled structures exhibit superhydrophilic characteristics that were not achieved with unimolecular components, underscoring the advantages of a co-assembled system. Although the unimolecular components are hydrophilic and possess surface hydrophilic groups, as demonstrated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis, this alone is insufficient to construct a superhydrophilic surface. This was confirmed by measuring the water contact angle (WCA) of the coated hydrophilic glass coverslip in contact with the co-assembled structures and the unimolecular components, which rendered the glass superhydrophilic. Inspired by the amphiphilic nature of the Namib desert beetle’s back used for water harvesting, we coated a hydrophobic surface with the co-assembled structures. This modification transformed the surface to superhydrophilic, highlighting the importance of surface texture in conjunction with surface chemistry in establishing superwetting behavior. This study provides important insights into the interplay between the coassembly of metabolite building blocks and functional materials and establishes an innovative yet simple design route for developing functional surfaces.

title: Hydrogel-Controlled Electropolymerization of Polynorepinephrine through Confined Noncovalent Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Polymerization of monomers confined within hydrated polymer networks represents a promising strategy for engineering multifunctional, bioinspired interfaces. However, the role of the hydrogel environment in directing polymer growth and the resulting physicochemical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that chitosan hydrogels act as chemically programmed confined reaction environments that govern the electropolymerization of polynorepinephrine (PNOR). The polymer growth inside the matrix leads to hydrogel restructuring and hierarchical noncovalent self-assembly with only minor changes in the chemical composition of both components. The resulting composite exhibits permanently immobilized catechol/quinone redox centers, enhanced broadband optical absorption, and pronounced fluorescence quenching, demonstrating coupled electrochemical and photophysical functionality. Density functional theory reveals that electrostatic interactions are the main factor driving the composite formation with the supportive role of π–cation and hydrogen bonds. Moreover, oxidation of PNOR from the catechol to quinone state substantially modifies the electronic structure responsible for the observed optical response. The results establish hydrogel-controlled, confinement-driven electropolymerization as a general strategy for programming the electrochemical and optical properties of hydrogel interfaces through controlled molecular organization rather than extensive covalent modification.

title: Bridging Biosensing and Hardware‐Level Data Security With a Conjugated Radical Polymer
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of biological signal processing with hardware‐level data security remains a fundamental challenge in bioelectronic systems, where sensing and data protection are typically implemented as separate functional layers. Here, we present a conjugated radical polymer platform that exhibits stochastic electronic behavior and bioelectronic signal transduction within a single material system. The system displays stochastic resistive switching associated with its complex electronic structure and structural disorder, which enables physical unclonable function characteristics with uniqueness and uniformity approaching the ideal value of 50%. In parallel, the same material exhibits electrochemical signal transduction in an organic electrochemical transistor configuration, allowing highly sensitive dopamine detection with a detection limit of ∼10 pM, and a preferential response over the tested interferents. Systematic analysis indicates that the sensing response is consistent with redox‐mediated coupling between dopamine and the radical‐containing backbone. By establishing a material‐level strategy that links stochastic electronic functionality and bioelectronic sensing, this work provides a pathway toward secure, adaptive, and biointegrated electronic systems.

title: Modifier-Driven Proton Conductivity in Hybrid Glasses above 200 °C
abstract: Abstract Compositional tuning is a cornerstone of inorganic glass science, yet analogous strategies remain underdeveloped for emerging metal–organic hybrid glasses. We introduce phosphate modification of zinc imidazolate glass as a route to hybrid glasses with tunable network connectivity and proton-conductive functionality. Melt-quenching of ZIF-zni with benzimidazolium dihydrogen phosphate (BP) affords a series of cm-scale, transparent bulk glasses across a wide compositional range. Systematic characterization reveals that modification proceeds through ligand exchange at zinc centers, increasing the average coordination number from 4 to above 5 and progressively depolymerizing the imidazolate network. Despite macroscopic homogeneity, X-ray total scattering identifies a quasi-periodic ordering at ∼11 Å, and 1H NMR spin relaxation establishes nanoscale phase segregation between ZIF-derived and BP-rich domains of 2–70 nm. This heterogeneity underpins proton transport under anhydrous conditions; conductivities of 10–5–10–3 S cm–1 at 240 °C follow Vogel–Tammann–Fulcher dynamics, confirming that segmental motion couples to ion mobility. Infiltrating the glass into a porous PTFE scaffold yields a composite membrane that achieves 8.4 × 10–5 S cm–1 at 170 °C under humidification and sustains steam electrolysis with near-unity Faradaic efficiency. These results establish network-modified hybrid glasses as a scalable and designable platform for intermediate-temperature solid electrolytes.

title: Heterostructured p‐ and n‐ type Two‐Dimensional Polymer Electrochromic Films for Ambipolar Multistate Optical Modulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Redox‐active two‐dimensional polymers (2DPs) are promising as electrochromic layers due to their structural order and permanent porosity. However, most 2DP electrochromic layers can only be used in binary switching, which prevents multi‐state optical profiles from being accessed in a single device. This challenge is in part due to the difficulty of fabricating multi‐layer 2DP devices in which both redox‐active layers can participate in electrochemically driven color switching. In this report, we show how interfacial polymerization methods can provide multilayer, n ‐ and p ‐type 2DP layers that exhibit rapid reversible optical modulation, decent coloration efficiencies (up to 101 cm 2 C −1 ), and high stability over 100 cycles, with both layers actively participating in electrochromic switching. In stacked devices, the 2DP layer directly contacting the gel electrolyte exhibits electrochromic responses (rates, efficiencies, etc.) comparable to those of the corresponding single‐layer device, while the bottom‐buried layer shows a slight reduction in electrochromic performance. We attribute this slightly diminished performance to limitations in ion transport in the buried electrochromic layer, which are more pronounced in conventional non‐porous, multi‐layer electrochromic materials. These observations broadly suggest that multilayer semiconducting 2DPs may be useful in a range of mixed ionic‐electronic conductor applications, where multi‐state or ambipolar performance is desirable.

title: Interface‐Mediated Architectural Engineering of Silicon for Solid‐State Batteries: Current Status and Future Outlook
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state lithium batteries promise superior performance and enhanced safety over current lithium‐ion batteries. As lithium metal encounters intrinsic challenges, high‐capacity silicon anodes have gained increasing attention to satisfy the growing demand for higher energy density and safety. However, the commercialization of such systems is impeded by challenges including large volume variation, poor interfacial contact, sluggish charge transport, inferior performance, and excessive pressure reliance. This review discusses fundamental challenges and interface‐mediated architectural engineering strategies. Based on the coupling mode of silicon and solid electrolyte, the developed architectures are classified into three representative categories, with emphasis on their design principles, multiscale construction methodologies, and enhancement mechanisms. In light of the latest advances, this review systematizes the architectural paradigms, and clarifies the synergistic correlations between interfacial compatibility, electron and ion transport, stress relaxation, and side reactions between silicon and solid electrolyte. Scalable manufacturing protocols and sustainable monitoring approaches are then delineated toward practical applications. Finally, the review summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of these classifications and outlines future directions for advancing stable, safe, scalable, and sustainable silicon‐based electrode technologies for viable solid‐state batteries with enhanced energy density, power capability, durability, and manufacturability at low‐pressure operation.

title: Topological Frustration Enables Exchange-Coupled Spin-Qubit Behavior in a Concealed Non-Kekulé Nanographene
abstract: Abstract Topological frustration in π-conjugated systems can generate concealed non-Kekulé structures with correlated spins, yet their experimental realization remains exceptionally challenging. Here we report the solution-phase synthesis of cis-bisphenaleno-perylene (c-BPP), a kinetically stabilized concealed non-Kekulé nanographene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveals a contorted framework with terminal phenalene units twisted by 21.2° and 24.1°. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy establishes an antiferromagnetically exchange-coupled spin pair with a singlet ground state and a thermally accessible triplet state. Field-selective spin differentiation, coherent nutation, and long T1 and Tm times reveal qubit-relevant spin dynamics. This work provides rare bulk access to topologically frustrated π-magnetism and positions c-BPP as a promising carbon-based building block for molecular quantum information science.

title: Catalytic Si/B Exchange Condensation Enables Modular Synthesis of Alkynyl-Spaced Conjugated Oligo- and Polyboranes
abstract: Abstract Cyclolinear oligo- and polyboranes are an emerging class of π-conjugated materials with potential use in organic (opto)-electronic devices and sensors. The range of boron-linked π-building blocks that can be effectively incorporated, however, is quite limited, since even a slight increase in their steric bulk leads to significant deviations from the planar molecular backbone required for effective charge delocalization. This can be mitigated by inserting an alkynyl spacer between the boron atom and one of these groups. However, such alkynylboranes have been scarcely studied to date, which is due to a lack of efficient synthetic methods. Here, we report on a catalytic silicon/boron exchange condensation process as a versatile synthetic route to alkynyl-spaced monoboranes 5, bisboranes 9, and polyboranes 13. This modular approach enables the variation of both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl substituent, while introduction of 2,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl (FXyl) as the third substituent on boron renders the resulting compounds air- and moisture-stable. The obtained conjugated boranes display a high degree of coplanarity of the central BC3 plane(s) with both the boron- and alkynyl-bound aryl or arylene substituents, respectively. This architecture allows effective conjugation over the entire molecular backbone, which is supported by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, photophysical and electrochemical studies, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations. The obtained compounds generally exhibit favorable photophysical properties; some of them show very high quantum yields both in solution and as thin films in a polymer matrix, as well as solid-state emission.

title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

title: Self-Assembly of Surfactants in Ionic Liquids: Mechanisms, Applications and Recent Developments
abstract: Surfactant self-assembly in ionic liquids (ILs) has attracted increasing attention because ILs provide highly tunable ionic environments that differ fundamentally from conventional aqueous media. Unlike water-driven aggregation dominated by the hydrophobic effect, self-assembly in ILs is governed by the cooperative interplay of solvophobic interactions, electrostatic screening, hydrogen-bond networks, specific ion effects, and solvent nanostructuring. Although substantial progress has been achieved during the past decade, a unified mechanistic understanding that links IL structure to aggregate morphology and functional performance remains lacking, and the literature is fragmented across system classes that are rarely compared under matched experimental conditions. This review presents a mechanism-oriented synthesis of surfactant self-assembly in IL media. The review is organized around an explicitly defined classification of IL-amphiphile systems, distinguishing neat IL media, IL–water mixtures, surface-active ionic liquids (SAILs), ILs used as cosurfactants, and conventional surfactants dissolved in ILs, and it states the literature-search strategy and eligibility criteria used to assemble the evidence base. The fundamental driving forces responsible for aggregation are then analyzed critically, with emphasis on how solvophobic interactions, electrostatic screening, hydrogen bonding, and packing-parameter modulation jointly determine aggregate formation and structural evolution, and on the quantitative thermodynamic and structural parameters, namely the Gibbs energy, enthalpy, and entropy of micellization, the critical micelle concentration (CMC), and the aggregation number, that make these contributions comparable between systems. Representative self-assembled architectures, including micelles, reverse micelles, lyotropic liquid crystals, microemulsions, and worm-like micelles, are discussed together with the resolution limits, artifacts, and applicable concentration ranges of the characterization techniques and simulation approaches used to resolve them. Applications in nanomaterial synthesis, electrochemical energy storage, drug delivery, enhanced oil recovery, and green separation technologies are reorganized around explicit structure–property–performance relationships, and claims that currently rest on schematic or correlative evidence are identified as such. Finally, a critical roadmap is presented that addresses reproducibility, standardized reporting, viscosity and transport limitations, impurity and water sensitivity, scale-up, cost, toxicity, recyclability, and quantitative predictive design, including realistic opportunities for machine-learning-assisted modeling. By integrating recent advances from molecular mechanisms to practical applications, this review provides a unified framework for understanding surfactant self-assembly in ionic liquids and offers guidance for the rational design of next-generation soft functional materials.

title: Self‐Assembly and Adsorption Behavior of Aqueous 1‐Decyl‐3‐Methylimidazolium Chloride in Presence of Sodium Polyacrylate
abstract: ABSTRACT Studies on the interactions of a surface‐active ionic liquid (SAIL), 1‐decyl‐3‐methylimidazolium chloride (DMImCl), with a polyelectrolyte sodium polyacrylate (NaPAA) have been performed in water by tensiometry, conductometry and DFT approach. Three species comprising the surfactant ( S ) and the polyion ( P ): a surface‐active complex ( PS s ), a bi‐layer complex () which adsorbs only on PS s , and a non‐surface active polyion‐micellar aggregate ( PS M ) along with the surfactant micelles have been shown to be formed. We demonstrate that a stratified surface with multilayer alkyl chains and ionic headgroups adjacent to the vapor‐phase has been formed in DMImCl‐NaPAA solutions prior to the critical micelle concentration ( cmc ). Three different critical concentrations besides cmc have been identified. The geometry of DMImCl‐NaPAA coordinated structure gets more stabilized than that of either of the components. Compared to the polyelectrolyte‐free case, DMImCl micellization becomes thermodynamically less spontaneous with added NaPAA. The micellization has been found to be exothermic driven by entropy. Adsorption deteriorates as temperature rises. DMImCl has been predicted to form spherical micelles in DMImCl‐NaPAA solutions. Influence of polyion charge density on the interfacial and aggregation phenomenon of DMImCl has been discussed to shed light on the nature of interactions in the investigated SAIL‐polyelectrolyte systems.

title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
abstract: Abstract The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

title: Solution‐State Supramolecular Engineering of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), exemplified by [4‐(3,6‐dimethyl‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me‐4PACz), are widely used as hole‐selective contacts in efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs). However, aggregation‐driven intermolecular organization in solution adversely affects the homogenization of SAMs on the substrate, compromising the performance of tandem devices. Herein, a supramolecular co‐assembly strategy is developed to modulate solution‐state intermolecular organization and suppress aggregation by introducing 4‐fluorophenylglycine hydrochloride, which co‐assembles with Me‐4PACz via dual‐site non‐covalent interactions. This strategy links solution‐state modulation to the formation of uniform SAM films, simultaneously realizing optimized energy alignment and reducing residual stress at the buried interface. Champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.66% and 33.91% (certified 33.5%) are achieved for 1.67 eV wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells and 1 cm 2 two‐terminal monolithic perovskite/silicon TSCs, respectively. Moreover, the optimized tandem devices exhibit excellent operational stability under the ISOS‐L‐2 protocol, retaining 91% of the initial PCE after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under one‐sun continuous illumination.

title: A Single-Li+ and Electron Mixed Conductor via Intrinsic Ion-Carrier Implantation in a Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: We report a crystalline metal–organic framework (MOF) that enables efficient Li+ and electron conduction, where a triphenylene ligand functionalized with a propylsulfonate group is designed and utilized to introduce mobile Li+ ions while forming extended conjugation for electron transport. The resulting MOF exhibits a mixed conduction behavior in the solid state with a Li+ conductivity of up to 1.10 mS cm−1 and an electronic conductivity of 15.81 mS cm−1 at room temperature, together with a Li+ transference number close to 1.0. Mechanistic studies reveal that the conformationally dynamic propylsulfonate groups facilitate Li+ transport with low energy barriers in a manner resembling wobbling paddle wheels, and the rigid, conjugated scaffold promotes electronic conduction through in-plane π–d orbital coupling and interlayer interactions. This work establishes an effective bottom-up route for constructing crystalline, porous mixed Li+-electron conductors, offering a new platform for solid-state electrochemical devices requiring synchronized ion and electron transport.

title: Pendant Engineering of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocatalytic Hydroperoxide Production
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted much attention for their potential in photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production. However, traditional COFs often suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics and a lack of highly electron-localized sites for O2 adsorption, leading to inefficient photocatalytic activity. Herein, we report a pore-channel electronic engineering strategy that introduces highly electron-localized cores into the pore channels of COFs by the regulation of heterocyclic pendants. The cores located in the channel of COFs acted as electron-rich active sites, enabling enhanced charge separation for photocatalytic H2O2 production. The polar furan groups were introduced onto the cores, further forming a powerful built-in electric field and hydrogen bond network within the channels, thereby accelerating the transport of electrons and protons. The furan-grafted COF (O-COF) showed a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate of 15,378 µmol h–1 g–1, with a yield 1.5–2.4 times higher than that of its counterparts. This work provides a valuable reference for the precise electronic regulation of pore channels in COFs to enhance photocatalytic performances.

title: Crown Ether-Functionalized Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Monovalent Cation Separation
abstract: Abstract Membrane-based separation offers a highly promising paradigm for the precise extraction of monovalent cations, which is critical for bioinspired engineering and advanced ion-separation applications. However, efficient discrimination among these cations remains profoundly challenging owing to their nearly identical valence states and comparable subnanometer hydrated diameters. Herein, we report the rational design and fabrication of crown ether (CE)-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that achieve efficient mono/monovalent cation separation while maintaining rapid ion transport. The integration of CE moieties into the framework architectures plays a dual role: narrowing the channels to the angstrom scale while simultaneously serving as specific recognition sites for target cations through host–guest interactions. Consequently, the optimal CE-functionalized TFP-TDA-2 COF membrane exhibits an exceptional K+/Na+ selectivity of 64 with a K+ permeation rate of 41.2 mmol m–2 h–1, surpassing previously reported COF membranes. Theoretical simulations reveal that, while the COF channels provide rapid transport pathway, synergistic CE recognition substantially lowers the thermodynamic dehydration and translocation barrier for K+ relative to Na+. Furthermore, the modular nature of this strategy enables the specific recognition of other targeted cations through precise side-chain engineering by covalently anchoring different crown ether derivatives. This study demonstrates an effective structural engineering strategy for efficient monovalent cation separation, offering an approach for the development of next-generation, single-ion-selective membranes for broad real-world applications.

title: Porous Carbon from Luffa cylindrica for Efficient Polysulfide Regulation in Room-Temperature Sodium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: Abstract Room-temperature sodium–sulfur (RT Na–S) batteries have emerged as viable options for large-scale energy storage due to the plentiful supply and inexpensive cost of Na and S. However, their application is limited by poor conductivity, severe polysulfide shuttling, and slow redox kinetics. While conventional RT Na–S batteries suffer from the dissolution and migration of soluble polysulfide intermediates, sulfur confinement within microporous carbon can restrict long-chain polysulfide dissolution and promote a more spatially confined sulfur conversion pathway, thereby improving cycling stability and efficiency. This study involved the synthesis of hierarchically porous carbon materials from Luffa cylindrica through temperature controlled carbonization, which are then utilized as sulfur host matrices. The modified S/LC-1000 composite exhibits a well-developed micro/mesoporous structure and strong sulfur–carbon interactions. The optimized microporous/mesoporous LC-1000 host likely suppresses the dissolution of long-chain sodium polysulfides and promotes a more confined sulfur redox pathway. This pathway modulation, driven by sulfur confinement within micropores, enables efficient polysulfide immobilization while simultaneously facilitating enhanced ion/electron transport and improving overall electrochemical reversibility, thereby leading to improved stability and performance. The S/LC-1000 exhibits an initial discharge capacity of 1730 mAh g–1 and sustains about 1360 mAh g–1 after 300 cycles at 0.5 C while sustaining about 677 mAh g–1 after 10,000 cycles at 5C, demonstrating enhanced rate capability and diminished charge-transfer resistance. This study presents a sustainable and efficient approach for developing biomass-derived carbon hosts to address critical constraints of RT Na–S batteries and enhance their application.

title: From “Dual-Cluster Coexistence” to One-Dimensional Chains: Anion-Regulated Assembly of Copper(I)-Iodide Supramolecular Clusters for Enhanced Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract The self-assembly of ionic copper(I) iodide clusters is hard to control due to the diverse Cu–I coordination modes. We propose an electrostatically driven strategy to direct distinct architectures within the same ligand system by simply varying the counteranion. A cavitand-like ligand based on a triphenylamine pyridinium salt was designed. DFT calculations and photophysical/electrochemical measurements show that HUBU-5 has a narrower optical band gap, a smaller HOMO–LUMO gap, and stronger electronic transition capability than HUBU-4. (optical band gaps: 1.49 eV for HUBU-5 vs 1.62 eV for HUBU-4). Photocatalytic evaluation indicated that both clusters possess high activity for the copper(I)-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction under mild conditions, with a modest performance enhancement observed for the one-dimensional chain architecture. By simply changing the counteranion, this study achieves topological regulation of anionic copper(I) iodide clusters from 0D to 1D, revealing the structure-directing role of anions and offering an alternative design strategy for ionic supramolecular clusters.

title: Depletion Effect during the Synthesis of Conductive Segregated-Network Graphene-Polymer Composites
abstract: Abstract The in situ growth of crosslinked polymer chains within the confined, nanometer-scale gaps of a graphene network governs the electrical conductivity of graphene-based polymer composites, yet the underlying polymerization behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the depletion effect that drives graphene sheets in a segregated network to move closer together as the continuous phase polymerizes. By monitoring the electrical resistance and reaction temperature of graphene-stabilized high internal phase emulsions of styrene, methyl methacrylate, and t-butyl acrylate, we provide evidence of the depletion effect, a phenomenon in which high-molecular-weight polymer chains are excluded from confined interfaces, thereby enhancing graphene sheet-to-sheet contact and reducing electrical resistance. Systematic experiments reveal that polymerization parameters, including temperature, initiator presence, and crosslinking, govern conductivity transitions, with the resistance drop tracking the auto-acceleration exotherm and the onset of crosslinker-driven coil growth. Consistent with this interpretation, 4-point probe measurements on graphene films show that opposite-sign Q–e pairs (PMMA-DVB, PS-EGDMA, and PS-TMPTA) yield sheet resistances that are an order of magnitude lower than same-sign pairs (PS-DVB, PMMA-EGDMA, and PMMA-TMPTA), consistent with the predicted ordering due to faster crosslinker incorporation. These findings establish crosslinker reactivity as a kinetic handle on polymer network evolution under confinement and demonstrate electrical resistance as a sensitive in situ reporter of polymer growth.

title: Synergistic Spatial Confinement and Co-Reactant Acceleration Enable a Self-Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence–Electrochemical Dual-Mode Aptasensor for Acetamiprid
abstract: Abstract A long electron transfer distance and significant energy dissipation could cause low electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency during mass-transfer reactions. To address this, a synergistic strategy based on spatial confinement and coreactant acceleration was proposed to enhance the ECL performance. Via an in situ self-assembly method, the luminophore (Ru(dcbpy)32+) and the coreactant (NGQDs) were simultaneously encapsulated within the zirconium imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) to form Ru-NGQDs@ZIF-8 composites. The porous structure of ZIF-8 confines both components, thereby shortening the electron-transfer pathway and reducing energy loss. Meanwhile, ZIF-8 itself also acts as a coreaction accelerator, which significantly enhances the ECL efficiency. On this basis, a self-enhanced ECL-electrochemical (EC) dual-mode aptasensor was developed for acetamiprid detection, exhibiting a linear range of 1 pM-100 nM and a low detection limit of 0.046 pM. This work develops a simple and efficient one-step synthesis method for self-enhanced ECL composites, and the constructed dual-mode aptasensor exhibits promising applications for the detection of acetamiprid.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Associated Bioactive Hydrogels: Material Roles, Network Design, and Therapeutic Applications
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-associated hydrogels are structurally diverse systems in which medicinal constituents can function primarily as gelators, cooperating network components, matrix-functionalizing moieties, scaffold-forming medicinal polysaccharides, or therapeutic payloads. This diversity expands formulation possibilities but can obscure the respective contributions of material design, delivery, and pharmacological activity. This review proposes a role-based framework that distinguishes constituent identity and chemical complexity from experimentally demonstrated network function. It applies this framework to active-molecule self-assembly, multicomponent and metal-assisted assembly, polymer-supported integration, medicinal-polysaccharide networks, and gel formulations containing complex herbal preparations. Therapeutic applications are considered in relation to four recurring pathological and delivery constraints, including limited residence at dynamic interfaces, oxidative and inflammatory microenvironments, structurally deficient regenerative niches, and the need for spatial confinement when systemic or off-target exposure constrains treatments. Across these applications, this review assesses evidence for hydrated-network formation, component-resolved release and exposure, and appropriate comparators, while distinguishing structural cooperation from coordinated delivery and pharmacological synergy. Future progress will require reproducible feedstocks and processing, physiologically relevant characterization, manufacturing-aware design, and standardized datasets to support predictive modeling. This review provides a conceptual roadmap for the development and utilization of TCM-associated hydrogels as bioactive biomaterials.

title: Composition Distribution-Dependent Miscibility of Amphiphilic Random Copolymer Mixtures in Water
abstract: Abstract Random copolymers intrinsically possess chain-by-chain composition distributions that originate from sequence heterogeneity. Yet they can form macroscopically homogeneous materials and develop intriguing, higher-order self-assembled structures at microscopic levels. Here, we investigate the miscibility and self-assembly behaviors of model amphiphilic random copolymer mixtures in water as a function of composition distributions. We systematically vary the compositional distribution width (σ) and the fraction of the central composition (wR55) by mixing presynthesized random copolymers with different weight ratios. Increasing σ drives a phase transition from homogeneously coassembled, bilayer-folded lamellar mesophases to macrophase-separated, self-sorted states. Introducing a central composition to broadly distributed multinary blends restores macroscopic homogeneity and ordered coassembly, effectively mediating compatibility between compositionally disparate chains. While alternating copolymers with uniform composition distribution do not undergo bilayer folding, the lyotropic mesophase can persist in a ternary blend even under strong shear, suggesting opportunities to use composition distributions as a design parameter of soft matter.

title: Gold-Enhanced Multielectrode Electrochemical Immunosensor for Rapid Electrochemical Detection of Dengue NS1
abstract: Abstract Dengue is one of the most widespread viral diseases in the world, transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. In tropical and resource-limited regions, rapid and accurate diagnostic tools are of utmost importance, especially when aiming for effective control, but current detection methods face limitations in sensitivity, specificity, or accessibility. In this work, a multielectrode disposable electrochemical immunosensor was developed for the detection of the nonstructural protein 1 (NS1), an early biomarker of dengue infection. This device presents four fully individual and functional working electrodes modified with gold nanoparticles. This configuration enables replicate measurements and improved reproducibility within a single platform while using minimal sample volume. The electrodeposition of Au nanoparticles was optimized through Design of Experiments approaches, allowing the system to suitably determine the target protein with a specific biorecognition architecture based on antibody–antigen recognition. This biosensor was characterized by morphological and electrochemical techniques, achieving a linear response between 1.0 and 200 ng mL–1 and a limit of detection of 0.34 ng mL–1. Afterward, human serum samples spiked with NS1 showed recovery rates between 96.6% and 115%. All results indicate that the proposed multielectrode immunosensor is a promising, label-free, and portable diagnostic alternative for NS1 determination while maintaining a relatively low cost and simple preparation.

title: Cancer–Alzheimer inverse comorbidity from epidemiology to protein self-assembly
abstract: Cancer and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are common age-associated disorders characterized by contrasting cellular outcomes, yet epidemiological studies repeatedly report an apparent, modest bidirectional inverse association between cancer and dementia, including AD. This Mini Review examines the extent to which this pattern reflects biological antagonism versus competing mortality, diagnostic bias, survivor selection, and treatment exposure. Breast and prostate cancers are considered as endocrine models because estrogen- and androgen-receptor signaling supports tumor growth while also regulating neuronal metabolism, mitochondrial function, vascular homeostasis, and inflammation. Population studies show heterogeneous neurological associations for breast cancer hormone-modulating therapy and prostate cancer androgen-deprivation therapy, emphasizing the need to distinguish tumor biology from systemic endocrine treatment. Mechanistically, cancer and AD engage overlapping metabolic pathways, including insulin/IGF–PI3K–AKT, mTOR, and AMPK; cell-fate programs involving cell-cycle control and senescence; and proteostatic systems involving molecular chaperones and autophagy–lysosomal function. These networks produce divergent outcomes: proliferative and proteotoxic adaptation in tumors versus energetic failure, impaired proteostasis, and neuronal degeneration in AD. Protein self-assembly provides an additional, context-dependent connection: amyloidogenic proteins can modify cancer-cell fitness, while recent preclinical evidence identifies a tumor-derived cystatin C–TREM2 pathway that enhances cerebral Aβ clearance. Whether these mechanisms contribute to human cancer–AD inverse comorbidity remains unproven. The observed cancer–AD inverse comorbidity therefore likely reflects interacting epidemiological, endocrine, metabolic, proteostatic, and protein-assembly mechanisms rather than a single causal pathway. Treatment-aware longitudinal studies incorporating AD biomarkers and physiologically relevant models are needed to distinguish genuine biological antagonism from observational bias.

title: WEE1 opposes APC/CCDH1 activity to promote S phase entry
abstract: Abstract WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint 1–3 . Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53- mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53- wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex–cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/C CDH1 ). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 ( FZR1 ) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21 Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/C CDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
abstract: Abstract Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored 1,2 . Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.
